monthly_review.summary: This month shows a deliberate shift toward lower-intensity, higher-volume aerobic development — evidenced by increased Z1 time and reduced average HR — though at the cost of some pace consistency and aerobic training effect compared to last month.
monthly_review.highlight: Zone 1 time jumped from 23% to 39% while Zone 3+ dropped from 45% to 17%, indicating a strategic aerobic base-building shift — but it coincided with a 26 sec/km slowdown and a 0.4-point drop in average aerobic training effect.

goal_tracker.message: You need 0.2 more km across 1 session in the remaining 6 days to match last month’s distance — easily achievable with a short 2–3 km recovery run; also aim for 1 more run to equal last month’s session count.

insights.title: Efficiency dip despite cadence gain
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency declined from 13.66 to 13.39 km/hr per bpm, even as cadence rose from 142 to 145 spm — suggesting improved turnover isn’t yet translating to better oxygen-cost-per-km, likely due to increased vertical oscillation (avg +0.3 cm this month) and longer ground contact times on slower runs.

insights.title: Strong Z1 emphasis, minimal high-intensity work
insights.body: Z1 now comprises 39% of total time (up from 23%), while Z4+ is virtually absent (1% vs 19% last month), confirming a dedicated low-HR aerobic phase — however, Z3 remains at 16% (down from 26%), meaning threshold stimulus has meaningfully decreased.

insights.title: Form variability under pace stress
insights.body: On the 2.5 km run at 7:27/km (447 sec/km — your best pace), stride length surged to 94.35 cm (+23 cm vs monthly avg) and ground contact dropped to 286 ms (−27 ms vs monthly avg), showing neuromuscular readiness — but vertical oscillation rose to 8.1 cm (+0.5 cm above monthly avg), hinting at inefficiency at faster efforts.

insights.title: Reduced cumulative aerobic stimulus
insights.body: Average aerobic TE fell from 3.1 to 2.7, and total runs dropped from 9 to 8 — despite similar weekly volume, the lower intensity and fewer sessions reduced overall adaptive signal, particularly for lactate clearance and capillary density development.

recommendations.action: Do one 5 km run at Zone 2 HR (130–138 bpm) with cadence ≥148 spm and focus on landing midfoot to reduce ground contact time — target <305 ms based on your 3.8 km run on 5/13 (309 ms) and 3.5 km run on 5/22 (308 ms).
recommendations.reason: Your two most efficient recent runs (5/13 and 5/22) had cadence ≥150 and ground contact ≤309 ms — replicating that combo at Zone 2 will reinforce aerobic neuromuscular patterning without overstressing HR.

recommendations.action: Insert one 12-minute Zone 3 interval session: 3 × 4 min @ 148–154 bpm (matching your 2.5 km effort on 5/16), with 90s walk/jog recovery — keep stride length ≤85 cm to limit vertical oscillation.
recommendations.reason: Your Z3 time dropped sharply (16% vs 26% last month), and your 2.5 km run at 148 bpm shows you can sustain Zone 3 effectively — reintroducing controlled threshold work will preserve VO₂ max (stable at 37.0) and boost aerobic efficiency.

recommendations.action: Add a 15-minute post-run mobility routine focused on hip flexor release and calf elasticity after your next two runs — especially following any session where vertical oscillation exceeded 7.8 cm (e.g., 5/16 at 8.1 cm).
recommendations.reason: Vertical oscillation increased on faster efforts and correlates with stiffness — your 5/16 run showed highest VO₂ max maintenance (37.0) but also highest vertical oscillation (8.1 cm), suggesting elastic energy return is suboptimal.

weekly_focus.description: Balance low-HR endurance with targeted neuromuscular reinforcement — prioritize rhythm, footstrike timing, and elastic recoil at Zone 2, while reintroducing brief, precise Zone 3 efforts to maintain metabolic resilience.
suggested_sessions: 5 km Zone 2 run with cadence ≥148 spm and ground contact <305 ms
3 × 4 min Zone 3 intervals (148–154 bpm) w/ 90s recovery
